title: A final indexing object computes a coherent colimit
statement: An infinity category means a simplicial set with fillers for every inner horn, where an inner horn is the union of the faces of the standard simplex except one face other than the first or last. The standard simplex $\Delta^n$ is the nerve of $\{0<\cdots<n\}$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Colimits are understood in the coherent mapping-space sense: a cocone with vertex $L$ is a colimit when, for every object $T$, composition induces an equivalence from $\operatorname{Map}(L,T)$ to the space of coherent cocones with vertex $T$. Let $J$ and $\mathcal C$ be infinity categories, let $t$ be a final object of $J$, meaning that $\operatorname{Map}_J(j,t)$ is contractible for every object $j$ of $J$, and let $p:J\to\mathcal C$ be a functor. Then $p$ has a colimit with vertex $p(t)$. One can choose its cocone so that its edge at $t$ is the identity of $p(t)$. In particular, for every $n\geq0$ and every diagram $p:\Delta^n\to\mathcal C$, its value $p(n)$ at the last vertex is a colimit, with the cocone induced by the order-preserving map $[n+1]\to[n]$ which fixes $0,\ldots,n$ and sends $n+1$ to $n$.
